evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run monthly immunization camps in 40 villages in Rajasthan. Baseline survey of mothers of children under two, read aloud in Hindi or Marwari by female enumerators; most mothers have 0 to 5 years of schooling. Constructs from our measurement plan: (a) attendance: whether the mother brought the child to the camp held in her village last month; (b) perceived difficulty of getting to the camp, meaning time, distance, and needing permission, which we want as separate things; (c) her expectation of how many other mothers in the village attend; (d) intention to attend next month's camp. The block is 8 questions at most. Write the items.
evals.expected_output: Draft survey questions in the output template for all four constructs, with the read-aloud script and the design check.
assertions: No question asks the respondent to agree or disagree with a statement.
Every rating question has its options in words and comes with a three-option version for mothers who cannot read.
Time, distance, and permission are asked in three separate questions.
Each question states what a correct reading is.
The attendance question names last month's camp, not what the mother usually does.
Says the questions are untested and does not offer to add them into a score.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Write some survey questions about savings for our program.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what about savings is to be measured and who the respondents are, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the constructs, or what exactly about savings the survey must measure.
Asks who the respondents are or how they will answer.
Does not write any survey question.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: HIV self-testing program in Lagos, follow-up survey with young men 18 to 29 who received a kit, read aloud by male enumerators in Yoruba or English. Constructs: (a) kit use: whether he used the kit in the last 3 months; (b) partner count: number of sexual partners in the last 3 months, which is one of our two main outcomes; (c) perceived stigma: how he thinks people in his area view someone who tests. Max 8 questions. Write them.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes questions for kit use and perceived stigma, leaves the partner count unwritten, and tells the user to consult a survey methodologist.
assertions: Writes at least one question each for kit use and perceived stigma.
Does not write a direct question on the number of sexual partners.
Lists the partner count under 'Not written here' and says it needs a private or indirect method.
Tells the user to consult a survey methodologist or a specialist in measuring sexual behavior.
Says what to bring to that specialist.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our eight items on household decision-making for women in Bihar are drafted and we are happy with the wording. Can you check whether the women will understand them? We can interview eight of them next week.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the questions already exist and the need is to test whether respondents understand them, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the questions already exist, so nothing needs writing.
Does not rewrite the items or produce draft survey questions.
